Question_text: Fig. 3.1 shows light entering a transparent block. The light enters the block at an angle θ to the normal and travels through the block until it meets the bottom surface. The angle between the ray in the block and the vertical side of the block is φ.
image: Fig. 3.1 (not to scale) shows a ray of light entering a transparent block from the top surface. The light ray enters at an angle θ to the normal (dashed line) drawn perpendicular to the surface. Inside the block, the ray is refracted, bending towards the normal. The angle between the refracted ray and the vertical side of the block is labeled φ. The ray then travels to the bottom surface, where it makes an angle of incidence 'i' with the normal to the bottom surface.

Parts.part_text: Light travels more slowly in the block than in air.
